title: Python SDK response serializers and streaming parse workflow
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Provide a developer-friendly, production-ready set of helpers in the Python SDK for converting model responses into typed objects (dataclasses or pydantic models) and for ergonomically parsing structured output from streaming endpoints. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and examples for: 1) a thin serializer/deserializer layer that maps JSON responses to typed models without forcing runtime heavy dependencies by default; 2) a streaming parser that incrementally builds typed objects as tokens arrive and emits stable partial events for consumer usage; 3) clear migration docs and runtime fallbacks for untyped legacy responses. Motivation: teams building Redwood-backed features need reliable typing and validation when they persist or post-process model outputs, but streaming and retry interactions currently make structured parsing fragile (partial JSON, truncated tokens, parse errors during retries).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a `serialize_response` and `deserialize_stream` public API with typed annotations
Support both dataclasses and pydantic model shapes; choice controlled by optional dependency flag
Streaming parser emits consistent partial events and a final validated typed object on stream completion
Graceful handling of parse failures: retry-safe behavior with clear error types and telemetry hooks
Comprehensive unit + integration tests (including simulated truncated streams, KV-cache triggered retries, and model-variant fallbacks)
Documentation page with migration guide and three worked examples (simple generation -> dataclass, chat stream -> pydantic schema, embeddings batch -> typed container)
No regression for existing untyped response patterns; backwards-compatible defaults
design_decisions: Default runtime does NOT require pydantic. Pydantic support sits behind an extras install `redwood-sdk[validation]`
Provide two serializer implementations: `light` (std lib dataclasses + marshaling helpers) and `strict` (pydantic for runtime validation and rich errors)
Streaming parser will operate as a state machine: header meta -> body events -> finalization. It will surface `PartialObject` intermediate events with best-effort fields filled
On parse failure mid-stream: buffer until safe checkpoint, surface a `StreamParseError` with context, and allow configured retry semantics (retry request / skip / fallback to raw text)
Telemetry events: `sdk.typed_parse.start`, `sdk.typed_parse.partial`, `sdk.typed_parse.complete`, `sdk.typed_parse.error` to help correlate regressions with model changes
tasks: API design proposal: `serialize_response(obj_or_raw, model=..., mode='light'|'strict')` + `deserialize_stream(stream_iterable, model=..., config=...)`
Implement `light` dataclass serializer + helper that maps snake_case field names and optional aliases
Implement `strict` pydantic-backed serializer with clear validation error types
Streaming iterator implementation that yields (event_type, payload) tuples; provide an async and sync variant
Add feature toggles to SDK config to control default serializer and retry-on-parse-failure policy
Write end-to-end tests using recorded model responses and artificially truncated streams
Write migration docs and three example notebooks / code snippets
Add CI job coverage for both extras installed and bare installs to ensure optional deps behavior
